question: On the probe day, alone on the deployment, with payloads the size and shape of the recipe's: what is the largest in-flight count N* in {1, 2, 4, 8, 12} whose HTTP-429 share, exhausted-429 invocations and p95 invocation latency stay inside registered bounds, and what is its throughput gain G = rate(N*) / rate(1)? An engineering measurement of a transport; it decides nothing about any board, recipe, reference, judge or model; no verdict is read as data (1.1).

plain_description.what: Sends up to 398 synthetic judge requests to the grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning deployment at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12 parallel calls, measuring throughput, rate-limit errors and latency.
plain_description.why: Decides whether it is worth building a parallel caller to make judged runs faster; it says nothing about judge quality.
plain_description.information: A large speed-up would support parallel posting. None would keep runs sequential. Result: done. On one night, 12 parallel calls ran about 10x faster than 1, with zero rate-limit errors. The registered falsifier fired: the good conditions of an earlier night had returned. The decision to build the parallel caller had already been taken by the author regardless of this result, so the probe measures the limit rather than deciding the build. 12 is a lower bound, measured on one night only and on the non-reasoning model only. It licenses no daytime run, where limits were much worse earlier.
